findings.title: Concurrent builds for the same index are no longer serialized
findings.body: BuildIndex now only locks cacheMu when inserting the finished index, while GetIndex (lines 60-68) only checks the cache and has no in-flight tracking. Two concurrent Search/search-init/watch-event calls for the same not-yet-cached NamespacedResource can therefore both invoke BuildIndex, both run the document builder, and for file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory path at line 97. This can fail with an index-exists/lock error, double-count IndexTenants, leak the overwritten index without Close, or corrupt startup/search behaviour; previously GetIndex blocked on the read lock while a build held the write lock. Per-key in-flight deduplication (or equivalent) is needed, not just a short cache-insert lock.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu.RLock, while BuildIndex now concurrently writes b.cache[key] under the write lock at lines 137-139 (and builds now run in parallel during startup and on-demand). Concurrent map iteration and map write is a Go data race and can trigger a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic or race-detector failures. TotalDocs should snapshot or read the cache under RLock.

findings.title: Parallel init workers share the outer err and counter without synchronization
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, every errgroup worker executes 'totalBatchesIndexed++' and '_, _, err = s.build(...); return err' using variables captured from the enclosing scope. With initWorkers > 1 these are unsynchronized concurrent writes/reads: the race detector will flag them, the indexed count can lose increments, and one namespace's build error can be overwritten by another worker's result before it is returned, so init may report success despite a failed namespace build (or report another worker's error). Each worker should use a local err variable and an atomic/mutex-protected counter.

findings.title: Postgres integration coverage for the changed startup path is disabled
findings.body: The PR adds an unconditional skip for postgres in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer, the integration test that exercises the storage-server target whose initialization this PR moves into NewResourceServer. Skipping it removes CI coverage for exactly the eager-init/startup behaviour on postgres and can hide a postgres-specific startup regression (the comment only says it fails in Drone but works locally). The failure should be diagnosed or tracked with a linked issue rather than silently skipped.
